title: Cost attribution for AI work
subtitle: Every token my agents spend is attributed to the work order that bought it.

stats.label: metered usage records tied to work orders

lede: AI work costs money per token, and a cost nobody can tie to a deliverable cannot be managed. AgentOS gathers usage from three sources. Hooks capture coding-agent transcripts. Managed seats emit signed, replay-safe usage events, each attributed to the model the provider reported, which is the model that actually ran. Planning a work order costs tokens too. A capture step binds the authoring of a work order to the exact native conversation where the planning happened, passing only private file references, so no transcript content crosses the tool boundary. On top of attribution sits a value measure, Validated Human-Equivalent Engineering Hours (Validated HEH).
quote: Cost informs strategy and must never silently block dispatch.
evidence: Cost attribution for AI work: 31,811 metered usage records tied to 246 work orders, every token placed on the work that bought it.
Engineering productivity metrics: a value measure rebuilt after 99.7 percent of the first version's headline turned out to be token spend.
Prompt caching analysis: cache reuse of 43-97% across seats on one work order over a 24-hour window.
author: Corey James
